excludes: Transport framing, decoder and backpressure work is owned by ai-streaming when that is the primary outcome.
Agent topology, memory architecture and evaluation design are owned by ai-agent-architecture.
Generic frontend feature implementation without the conversational trust boundary is owned by frontend-implement.
native_ownership.responsibility: Implement an end-to-end conversational AI product boundary with server-authoritative history, installed SDK protocol, safe rendering, tools/approval, persistence, cancellation and handoff.

provenance.claim_scope: AI SDK useChat transport and caller-owned input state

risk.rationale: chatbot-implement changes repository runtime behavior and therefore requires scoped authorization, safe external-effect boundaries and affected-path verification.

negative.prompt: Implement and test a raw SSE decoder, terminal event schema, abort propagation, bounded buffering and partial-result state for an existing model endpoint; the surrounding chatbot UI and persistence are already complete.
Design a product agent's state machine, least-privilege tools, approval authority, memory governance, evaluation and rollout without implementing the chat UI or repository changes.

positive.prompt: Implement a multi-tenant web chatbot with persisted authoritative history, installed AI SDK useChat/transport protocol, server-owned system/tools, streamed parts, safe Markdown and resumable interrupted generations.

Add chat tool approvals and human handoff. Approval must bind exact authorized parameters, duplicate/lost responses must not repeat an external action, attachments and conversations are tenant-scoped, and partial output is not marked complete.

assertions.criterion: Owns the conversational client/server, persistence, rendering and tool UX while leaving transport-only streaming and agent architecture to neighboring skills.
Inspects installed ai/UI packages and types, route/provider config, auth, persistence, tool contracts, rendering and tests from the fixture without inventing versions or files.

Defines authoritative history and request protocol, reconstructs trusted model input and tools server-side, verifies installed SDK capabilities, then implements rendering, persistence and failure behavior.

Rejects client system/tool/approval/assistant authority, validates allowed UI parts and conversation ownership, converts only trusted messages, uses caller-owned input/transport if installed, returns the installed streamText response method and sanitizes model output/URLs.
Tests forged roles/results/approvals, cross-tenant IDs, malformed parts, installed client/server protocol, missing tool results, unsafe HTML/URLs, concurrent tabs and authoritative persisted history.
Reports protocol/capability evidence, trust and rendering boundaries, tool/persistence behavior, exact checks and residual provider/reconnect/moderation risks.
Keeps SDK-specific method names behind installed capability checks and centralizes server-owned transcript/tool reconstruction instead of duplicating trust logic in UI components.

scenarios.prompt: A chat route forwards the browser's entire messages array directly to streamText, including client-created system, tool, approval and assistant roles. The UI uses an old useChat input/handleSubmit recipe and renders model Markdown with raw HTML. Implement the bounded repair.

assertions.criterion: Rejects forged tool/approval state, requires a server approval bound to exact recipient/resource/version and operation identity, and refuses blind replay after the disconnect.
Reconciles the provider-authoritative operation, makes duplicate tool delivery idempotent, records partial generation as interrupted, sanitizes HTML/URL output and never treats abort as rollback.

Requires persisted operation/result, one external side effect, approval audit binding, safe rendered DOM and caller-visible reconciled state rather than a successful reconnect or completed-looking text.
Separately reports external mutation evidence, interrupted generation, rendering rejection and any unresolved provider/handoff boundary without exposing sensitive content.

scenarios.prompt: A user approves sending a payment receipt, then changes the recipient in a forged tool message. The provider succeeds but the browser disconnects before the result, reconnect sends the tool again, and the partial assistant HTML contains a javascript URL. Explain and implement safe behavior.

assertions.criterion: Uses the skill-required repository stack-context step when execution is available, then derives project authority for ai-sdk from the lockfile, installed core/UI types and matching official docs; applies only the pinned hook/transport/message conversion/response APIs and treats migration separately. When execution is withheld, stating that required stack-context generation and underlying evidence are unavailable is sufficient without literal shell syntax, but it must not claim the step ran.
Checks ai core, UI adapter, React/runtime, provider adapter, route runtime and protocol compatibility together.
Avoids remembered AI SDK majors and obsolete recipes, recording capability evidence and a single migration seam.

scenarios.prompt: The repository pins an AI SDK line whose useChat manages input differently and whose streamText result has a different response helper than current documentation. An upgrade is not authorized.
